assumptionsAndDecisions.decision: Combine the two research findings into one plan rather than two, because the Jev program depends on the contract fix and shares the registry/gate surfaces.
assumptionsAndDecisions.rationale: Avoids duplicated registry/corpus/gate tasks and orders Jev work after the enabling fixes.

observations: Two schema-valid research findings underpin this plan: the validated audit and the Jev deep-embedding finding.
Repo gates at HEAD: check-suite OK; validate-corpus-v2 94/0; payload drift 0; regen verifyFresh ok.
Live Jev probes (2026-09-26): state/instructions missing cause HTTP 400; batched mixed questions return typed answers.

design.approach: Grouped, dependency-ordered tasks with non-overlapping write ownership per parallel group; security and gate fixes precede the Jev service; trust schemas come last and only after registry coverage.
design.summary: Fix enabling defects first (security, gates, registry, contracts), then build the Jev program on top of a repaired provider and a gated corpus, and close with one aggregate acceptance gate.

discoveredRequirements.requirement: The 6 production schema ids and the missing compatibility pairs must be registered before trust-schema work.
The provider contract must be repaired before any embedding or parity test.

constraints: Jev stays optional and off by default; absent/disabled/failing behavior is byte-identical to today.
Every acceptance, security, completion, closure, receipt, digest, cursor, isolation, and commit decision stays deterministic and never-Jev.
Each task has one positive runnable acceptance signal; no disjunctive or deferral signals.
Tasks remain pending; this planning invocation authorizes no implementation.
deliverables: Security fixes: Docker credentialsNone, egress encoding/audit/bounds, bypass run-lease.
Gate and corpus completeness: payload metadata drift, full corpus gating, registry/compat coverage.
Contract reconciliation across csm-scan, csm-review, csm-review-python, csm-upload, csm-bdd-tdd, csm-deep-research, csm-plan.
Jev program: contract repair, live parity, shared decision service, new safe points, coverage/budget/telemetry, calibration program, trust-ladder schemas.

Additional adversarial findings: trace evidence substrate, csm-browse packaging/portability/hermetic tests, producer descriptor lockstep, hardcoded-path removal, drop-capture fail-closed, csm-build /1 evaluator decision, CI canary hardening.
exclusions: Implementing any of these tasks during this planning invocation.
Promoting Jev to any acceptance/security/completion gate (L5 refused).
Changing frozen /1 schemas beyond additive dual-accept.
goal.goal: Remediate every validated defect from the adversarial system audit AND embed Jev deeply as an optional, excessive-where-viable classifier, as one executable plan.
